ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl:
Assume n>1 and t are such that floor(k t)=k-1 for every integer k with 1<=k<=n. In particular, for k=n we get floor(n t)=n-1. By definition,
E_n(t)=floor(n t)-\sum_{k=1}^n floor(k t)/k
=(n-1)-\sum_{k=1}^n (k-1)/k.
Now (k-1)/k=1-1/k for each k, so
\sum_{k=1}^n (k-1)/k = \sum_{k=1}^n 1 - \sum_{k=1}^n 1/k = n-H_n,
where H_n=\sum_{k=1}^n 1/k is the n-th harmonic number. Therefore
E_n(t)=(n-1)-(n-H_n)=H_n-1.
This is exactly the claimed conclusion.
